facts.text: BendWire-v0 is registered with entry point gym_agx.envs:BendWireEnv, n_substeps=2 and max_episode_steps=1000
The action space is Box(-1, 1) with one element per velocity-controlled end-effector constraint
The default right gripper has three velocity-controlled translation constraints (x, y and z) and a hinge constraint that is not velocity-controlled, so its action vector has three elements
The action time step is the AGX simulation time step times n_substeps
The BendWire scene builder sets TIMESTEP to 1/100 s (100 Hz) and N_SUBSTEPS to 2
The reward is dense with range -1.5 to 1.5, success when the curvature distance is below 0.05, and success does not end the episode

The dense reward is the negative curvature distance clipped to the configured reward range, or the upper reward bound minus 100 times the end-effector speed clipped to zero and the upper bound when the goal is reached
Rewards are rounded with np.round(..., decimals=4)
Success means the curvature distance is below the configured threshold
step() returns the legacy Gym tuple observation, reward, done, info
reset() restores the start scene and returns a fresh observation
The default observation configuration adds DLO curvature and end-effector position observations, with DLO curvature and end-effector velocity as goals
The observation is a dict with observation, achieved_goal and desired_goal
construct_space gives every numpy observation leaf a Box with infinite bounds
The right gripper's max_velocity is 10/1000 m/s and its max_acceleration is 10/1000 m/s^2
rescale_velocity limits the speed change per call to max_acceleration*dt and clamps the speed to max_velocity
The goal assembly is added from the goal scene file and a randomized goal is sampled only when randomized_goal is set
The BendWire cable is declared with LENGTH 0.1 m, RADIUS as LENGTH/100, LENGTH increased by 2*RADIUS, and RESOLUTION 1000 segments per metre
get_cable_curvature allocates cable_segment_edges.shape[1] - 2 values, one per adjacent pair of cable segments
AgxGoalEnv.__init__ calls self.seed(); the class defines no seed method of its own, so the method comes from its external Gym base
The README describes the package as the OpenAI Gym interface for the AGX Dynamics simulation software
The environments import AGX Dynamics and raise DependencyNotInstalled without it

determinism.notes: the start scene and the default fixed goal are static, so a fresh environment repeats a run; the package fake seeds its Python RNG from reset(seed).  BendWireEnv.reset() takes no seed argument and the class defines no seed method of its own, so on the upstream sim backend cap.world.seed.v1 cannot be shown to reach AGX Dynamics; that path was not run

gaps: the package fake is a pure Python analytic stand-in, not AGX Dynamics: the cable, contacts, plasticity and the AGX solver are not modelled, and its curvature length, start state and goal arrays are placeholders

the real cable segment count and the saved scene state live in the binary gym_agx/envs/assets/bend_wire.agx file, which the package does not parse; the fake returns 8 curvature values while the device returns one per adjacent segment pair (about 100 for the 0.1 m cable at 1000 segments per metre), and AGX sets the exact count when it initializes the cable
the AGX time step is set by the scene builder to 1/100 s and BendWire-v0 runs n_substeps=2, so one action is 20 ms; the fake integrates one 20 ms step instead of two 10 ms AGX steps
no wall-clock pacing: realtime_factor 0, ticks advance simulated time by timestep_ms only
no physical device is modelled and the model was never validated against one
snapshot and restore are not offered: the environment exposes no get_state or set_state
the fake stores observations as Python lists; upstream returns numpy arrays built by construct_space

safe_state.description: the simulation stops advancing: no step or reset is accepted after an e-stop until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch; the environment state is kept and stays readable
